query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an α + β dual-phase alloy with low hardness and poor friction and wear properties under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Earlier studies explored redesigning the bulk alloy, which risks compromising its original advantages, and several surface-modification approaches. Traditional thermal spraying and thermal plating produced weak coatings with poor substrate bonding; composite coatings suffered from uneven constituent dispersion and weak interfaces; and laser cladding could generate intermetallic compounds, high residual stresses, cracks, and crazing. Prior refractory high-entropy-alloy studies reported improved hardness and wear resistance, but the broader requirements of compositional homogeneity, strong bonding, mechanical stability, and preservation of TC4’s beneficial properties remain. Formulate one neutral, testable hypothesis for an intervention that could satisfy these requirements. Specify the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Depositing a refractory high‐entropy alloy (RHEA) coating on TC4 using high-power impulse magnetron sputtering (HiPIMS) followed by a tailored low-temperature annealing step will form a nanocrystalline, compositionally homogeneous, and well‐bonded coating that significantly increases surface hardness and reduces friction and wear under extreme-contact stress conditions while preserving the beneficial bulk properties of TC4.
generation.material_initial_state: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) with its α + β microstructure, noted for low hardness and poor wear behavior under high-contact stress.
generation.intervention: Deposit a RHEA coating (e.g., a refractory MoNbTaW-based alloy) on TC4 using HiPIMS to ensure a uniform, dense film; subsequently, perform a controlled annealing treatment at approximately 500°C for 1 hour under an inert atmosphere to enhance bonding and relieve residual stresses.
generation.conditions: Tested in environments replicating extreme service: high-contact stress as applied by a pin-on-disc tribometer, sliding wear and friction measurements conducted at room temperature and elevated temperatures up to 500°C in an inert atmosphere to maintain coating stability.
generation.structural_mediator: A nanocrystalline, compositionally uniform RHEA coating with strong interfacial bonding to the TC4 substrate.
generation.mechanism: The multi-principal element composition and nanostructure of the RHEA impart a very high hardness and provide excellent resistance to plastic deformation. The annealing treatment promotes interfacial bonding without forming deleterious intermetallic phases. Together, these factors reduce surface friction and wear under high stress, effectively shielding the softer TC4 substrate while preserving its bulk advantageous properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated TC4, the coated and heat-treated samples are predicted to exhibit a significant increase in surface hardness and a reduction in both the friction coefficient and wear rate under high-contact stress conditions.
generation.baseline: Untreated TC4, which under similar test conditions shows low surface hardness, high friction, and rapid wear degradation.
generation.boundary: The improvements are expected to be effective up to the thermal stability limit of the coating (around 500°C) and under contact stress conditions that mimic the experimental setup. Beyond these limits, coating degradation or interface failure might occur.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of improvement (in percentage increase in hardness or reduction in wear rate) is uncertain and will depend on the fine tuning of the coating composition, deposition conditions, and annealing parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of TC4 substrates coated with the RHEA using HiPIMS, followed by annealing at 500°C for 1 hour in an inert atmosphere, and a control set of bare TC4. Subject both sets to tribometer tests (e.g., pin-on-disc) under high-contact stress with controlled loads at room temperature and at 500°C.
measurements: Coefficient of friction (via continuous friction monitoring during testing)
Wear rate (quantified by mass loss and/or wear scar measurements)
Coating adhesion quality (assessed via scratch tests)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the RHEA-coated and annealed samples do not show a statistically significant improvement (e.g., at least 10-20% increase in hardness and corresponding decreases in friction and wear metrics) compared to the control TC4 under the same test conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.
